evals.prompt: i've got a networking exam in 2 weeks. i know the basics like what an IP address is and what a router does, but TCP still confuses me. help me understand how TCP actually works
evals.expected_output: A Phase 1 map of TCP at one level of depth: definition, boundary, major components, and how they relate, with an ASCII diagram and a lettered menu. No step-by-step mechanisms yet. A learning record file is created.
expectations: Does not ask calibration questions before building the map, because the learner's level and goal are already stated
The response contains, in this order, a definition, a boundary, the major components, and the relationships between components
Names between 3 and 7 major components
Explains how at least two components interact with each other, rather than only listing components
Includes at least one ASCII diagram inside a fenced text block
Does not walk through step-by-step mechanisms such as the SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK exchange in the initial map
Ends with a menu that uses letters, with A to C naming specific components and D offering how the whole thing works
Creates a file named tafheem-<slug>.md in the working directory, where the slug refers to TCP
The created file contains the initial map and an exploration tracker listing every component as unexplored
